messages:
deploy-bot: Scheduling config-only rollout in change window 15:00-15:30 UTC. Changeset: tighten default tenant rate-limit 500->350 rps, global request timeout 18s->15s, routing policy: add 'latency-first' for eu-west/fr region, batching.max_tokens 2048->1024, prefix KV cache TTL 600->300s. Canary plan: 1% for 10m -> 10% for 15m -> 50% for 15m -> 100%. Auto-rollback triggers: 5xx rate increase >0.5% absolute OR p95 latency increase >2s OR token-cost unit >3%.

deploy-bot: Release notes: https://internal.redwood/release/2026-03-config-1742500000

a na: ACK — I'll monitor traces and latency. Heads-up: lowering KV TTL may increase eviction churn; watch kvcache_evictions and redis write latency.

liam: +1. I'm pinning the canary traffic to model-serving:v2.3.7-quant to avoid accidental model swaps during routing changes.

maya: Suggest excluding high-throughput tenants from initial canary: partner-x, internal-batch, analytics-ingest. We should not test on their traffic.

julian: ops checklist: release notes, ops-checklist, exclusion list applied, canary config pushed to deploy-bot. Also add a quick-playbook for manual rollback steps.

ops: I've added exclusions: tenant.exclude = ["partner-x","internal-batch","analytics-ingest"]. playbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/config-rollbacks

sre-oncall: Please set alerts: inference-node OOM, kvcache_evictions > baseline+10%, 5xx_rate > 0.3% (warning) and >0.5% (critical). Also trace sampling up for canary traffic.

ana: Adding metrics to watchdash: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, kvcache_evictions, token_cost_unit, cpu/gpu util per shard.

liam: small config snippet for canary pin (pasted for ops):
```
route:
  canary: 0.01
  pin_model: "model-serving:v2.3.7-quant"
exclude_tenants:
  - partner-x
  - internal-batch
  - analytics-ingest
batching:
  max_tokens: 1024
timeout_ms: 15000
kv_cache_ttl_s: 300
```

deploy-bot: Starting canary now — applying config to 1% of traffic. Canary window 10m begins.

deploy-bot: Canary 1% active.

ana: initial observations (1m in): p95 ~420ms, 5xx 0.02%, kvcache_evictions +2% — nothing concerning yet.

liam: no model-related anomalies. caches look healthy.

sre-oncall: added trace sampling for canary traffic. Watch memory on inference-nodes shard-3; I see a small uptick.

deploy-bot: Canary 1% window ended (10m). Metrics: p95 delta +35ms, 5xx delta +0.01%, kvcache_evictions +5%. All under rollback thresholds. Promoting to 10% for 15m.

maya: promote to 10% — holding exclusions. ops please capture timeline in the rollbook.

ops: document updated: INT-423 created for follow-up tuning of kvcache warmup.

deploy-bot: Canary 10% active.

ana: at 10% after 3m: p95 480ms, 5xx 0.03%, kvcache_evictions +12% (above baseline). No 5xx spike though.

sre-oncall: kvcache_evictions +12% flagged — but no OOMs and 5xx stable. Recommend continue but keep a close watch for sustained growth.

liam: agree. If eviction rate continues to climb >20% and correlates with p95 worsening, we'll roll back.

deploy-bot: Holding at 10% for 12 more minutes.

ana: telemetry note: token_cost_unit increased 1.8% — below the 3% guard.

deploy-bot: 10% hold complete. Metrics within guard rails. Rolling to 50% for 15m.

deploy-bot: 50% rollout started.

sre-oncall: saw a brief eviction spike coincident with 50% ramp start; evictions returned to ~15% over baseline within 2m. No 5xx change.

maya: ok to continue but schedule follow-up postmortem to adjust default KV TTL (consider intermediate 450s) and add warmup on startup.

ops: filing followup: INT-423 -> 'kvcache-warmup-and-ttl-adjust'. Assign to infra-team.

deploy-bot: Rolling to 100% now (final stage). Change window remains open until 15:30 UTC.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: 100% applied.

ana: post-roll metrics (5m): p95 530ms, 5xx 0.04%, kvcache_evictions +14%. Token cost +2.1%. All within configured rollback triggers.

liam: leaving pin in place for model-serving:v2.3.7-quant until next config cycle.

sre-oncall: no critical alerts fired. I'll keep 15m extended monitoring for the rest of the window.

ops: release notes updated with outcome and followups: https://internal.redwood/release/2026-03-config-1742500000#notes. INT-423 linked.

maya: follow-up action: update default kvcache_ttl to 450s in next patch and add a warmup hook for new nodes.

liam: sounds good. Closing this thread unless anyone has objections.

ana: no objections. thanks everyone :tada:

deploy-bot: Thread closed by deploy-bot. If any regression observed, use playbook to trigger manual rollback or ping #eng-oncall.
